title: Hom from bounded-above finite-free complexes preserves bounded-below acyclicity
statement: Let $(U,\mathcal O_U)$ be a ringed site [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], let $E^\bullet$ be a bounded-above cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose terms are finite-rank free $\mathcal O_U$-modules, and let $A^\bullet$ be a bounded-below acyclic cochain complex of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]. Then the total sheaf Hom complex $\mathcal H om^\bullet_{\mathcal O_U}(E^\bullet,A^\bullet)$ [def-pur-hom-complex] is acyclic.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 (Lemma 20.51.4, lemma-stalk-internal-hom), case (2), bounded-above locally free Hom calculation in the proof route

proof.text: Choose an upper bound $N$ for the degrees in which $E^\bullet$ is nonzero. In each bidegree, the component of the total Hom differential is the signed sum of the differential of $A^\bullet$ and precomposition with the differential of $E^\bullet$. By [lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact], applying $\mathcal H om(E^p,-)$ to every short exact sequence of cycles and boundaries in the acyclic complex $A^\bullet$ is exact; in coordinates this is the exactness of finite direct sums of sheaves.

source.place: Tag 0GM8, Lemma 20.51.4, case (2), finite locally free Hom calculation

proof.text: Since acyclicity of $\mathcal H om^\bullet(E^\bullet,A^\bullet)$ concerns its cohomology sheaves [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], it suffices to show that every section $z$ of degree $m$ with $d(z)=0$, over an object $V$ of the site, is locally a boundary. Choose a lower bound $M$ with $A^q=0$ for $q<M$. By [def-pur-hom-complex], $z=(z^p)_p$ with $z^p:E^p\to A^{p+m}$, and $z^p=0$ unless $M-m\le p\le N$, so only finitely many components occur. We seek $h=(h^p)_p$ of degree $m-1$, $h^p:E^p\to A^{p+m-1}$, with $d(h)^p=d_A h^p+(-1)^m h^{p+1}d_E=z^p$ for all $p$. Put $h^p=0$ for $p>N$ and descend. At stage $p$ the obstruction $w^p=z^p-(-1)^m h^{p+1}d_E:E^p\to A^{p+m}$ satisfies $d_A w^p=0$: this follows from the degree-$p$ component of $d(z)=0$, namely $d_A z^p=(-1)^m z^{p+1}d_E$, together with the equation already achieved at $p+1$. Since $A^\bullet$ is acyclic, $0\to B^{p+m-1}\to A^{p+m-1}\to B^{p+m}\to0$ and the identification of cycles with boundaries $Z^{p+m}=B^{p+m}$ are exact; by Step 1, $\mathcal H om(E^p,-)$ preserves the surjection $A^{p+m-1}\to B^{p+m}$, so after passing to a covering of $V$ there is $h^p$ with $d_A h^p=w^p$. For $p<M-m+1$ one may take $h^p=0$ (its target vanishes), so only finitely many refinements of the covering are needed. On the final covering, $d(h)=z$. Hence every cocycle section is locally a boundary, so all cohomology sheaves of the total sheaf Hom complex vanish and the complex is acyclic.
